transcript:
Meeting header
Date/Time: 2026-06-02 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Marcus Liu (Redwood CSM); Ava Reynolds (Nimbus VP Eng), Diego Morales (Nimbus SRE), Sofia Park (Nimbus Security), Liam O'Connor (Nimbus Product)

Summary (auto): Postmortem of 2026-05-31 cache eviction incident causing 1.5 hr service degradation. Discussed root cause, immediate mitigations, longer-term reliability improvements, and rollout plan for hotfix and Dedicated pilot.

00:00 Jordan Blake: all right good afternoon, everyone, thanks for joining, we know this is postmortem territory so we want to run quickly through what happened, who saw what, and then the fixes and next steps.
00:12 Ava Reynolds: thanks Jordan. appreciate you coordinating. Diego, do you want to start with what Nimbus saw on your side?
00:18 Diego Morales: yeah, sure. so on 05-31 at ~07:32 UTC we started seeing CPU and GPU tail latencies climb, requests started timing out to our app layer; it coincided with a burst of long context requests from a batch job — lots of 16k token calls — and the serving nodes started thrashing on KV cache.
00:36 Diego Morales: by 07:40 the autoscaler kicked but there was a spike in OOM and pod restarts, and the fallback to the backup model was slower than expected, causing about 75% of requests to see >2s extra latency.
00:52 Priya Shah: quick clarifying q, Diego — when you say KV cache thrashing, do you have eviction metrics? was it LRU eviction or forced eviction from memory pressure?
01:01 Diego Morales: mostly LRU churn, but also some forced page faults on GPU memory; our metrics show cache miss rates jumped from 3% to 28% during the window.
01:10 Priya Shah: okay that jives with what we saw in traces; the runtime's cache management hit a regression where certain prefix keys weren't being recognized for reuse (there was a hash mismatch in one of the kernel paths). we pushed a mitigation shortly after.
01:22 Jordan Blake: can you explain the mitigation and timeline?
01:25 Priya Shah: timeline — around 08:05 UTC Redwood pushed a config change to reduce KV cache size slightly to prevent OOMs and prioritized immediate evictions of very large prefixes, that stabilized node memory but increased latency. then at 08:28 we rolled a hotfix to fix the hash comparison bug in the runtime which restored prefix reuse behaviour; by 08:45 latency was back to baseline.
01:45 Ava Reynolds: so the hotfix fixed it. question — why didn't autoscaler spin up capacity sooner? were we constrained by reserved capacity thresholds?
01:53 Marcus Liu: good question — the autoscaler worked as designed but the burst was larger than the configured horizontal burst limits for your Dedicated-like pool; also the autoscaler has a cooldown configured which prevented immediate additional nodes. those configs are editable; we'll propose new settings.
02:10 Liam O'Connor: also from product side we want to understand how this affects our SLOs — our customers saw errors for about 12 minutes and degraded performance for ~90 minutes. we need an estimate of the likelihood of recurrence.
02:22 Priya Shah: short answer, bug introduced a rare code path where certain large prefix sequences caused mis-indexing; it's low probability but reproducible with curated request shapes. we're treating it as a high-severity reliability regression.
02:34 Sofia Park: on the security/compliance side we need assurance that logs/audit trails for the incident are preserved and that no sensitive payloads were cached improperly. can you confirm data retention during the incident and any cache leak risk?
02:47 Marcus Liu: Marcus here — we captured request-level telemetry and KV metadata; we looked for PII in caches — nothing indicates leakage of customer data. we'll provide the audit logs export and the SOC2 control excerpts.
03:00 Diego Morales: thanks — please send them. also, the fallback model you went to, was it a quantized variant? we saw some differences in output.
03:10 Priya Shah: yes the fallback path goes to a quantized 4-bit variant to preserve throughput under constrained memory; there can be slight quality diffs. part of the rollout plan will include output quality regression tests against your eval prompts.
03:22 Jordan Blake: let's capture immediate mitigations vs long-term improvements. immediate: hotfix to fix the hash mismatch, tuned autoscaler and burst settings, temporary increase in KV cache headroom for critical tenants?
03:35 Priya Shah: immediate we recommend — 1) apply runtime hotfix (we already built it, QA passed), 2) adjust autoscaler burst and cooldown for Nimbus account, 3) increase per-node GPU memory reservation to reduce forced evictions during spikes.
03:50 Ava Reynolds: for 2 and 3 we need the config changes and impact analysis. Diego will run soak tests before we accept.
04:00 Jordan Blake: long-term changes: 1) add unit/regression tests for large-prefix sequences to catch hash regressions, 2) improve observability on KV cache metrics (new dashboards + alerts), 3) staged rollout policy for runtime changes (canary + guardrails), 4) explore Dedicated pool pilot with pinned capacity to reduce cross-tenant interference.
04:24 Priya Shah: also looking at smarter eviction policies — maybe frequency-based or size-aware eviction rather than pure LRU for long-context workloads. and we'll add a runtime knob for immediate emergency cache reserve toggles.
04:36 Liam O'Connor: what's the timeline for the hotfix rollout to prod? and do we need downtime?
04:42 Priya Shah: hotfix is non-disruptive; we tested in canary and it rolls with zero downtime. plan: push to canary 2026-06-03, monitor 24h, then full rollout 2026-06-04 unless Canary shows issues.
04:58 Diego Morales: we'll run targeted load that reproduces the 16k token shape during canary window and share traces.
05:05 Jordan Blake: perfect. Marcus, you'll send the SOC2 snippet and logs?
05:09 Marcus Liu: yes I'll send an export link to the incident logs and the SOC2 excerpt by 2026-06-04.
05:14 Sofia Park: is there a remediation plan for cache retention policy? we need written assurance on how long keys persist and how KMS is used.
05:23 Marcus Liu: yes we'll include cache retention docs and KMS integration notes; none of the cached keys persisted to disk unencrypted.
05:31 Priya Shah: one more technical note — we also identified a scheduling edge where certain long-context infer threads could contend for the decoder queue; tuning the scheduler reduced tail latencies in internal tests. we'll include scheduler tuning recommendations for Nimbus.
05:46 Ava Reynolds: good. on contractual side, is this incident eligible for SLA credit?
05:50 Jordan Blake: we'll route that through your account team — Marcus will prepare the incident report and we can take SLA credit conversation offline with Nimbus finance.
05:59 Liam O'Connor: for quality assurance, can Redwood run the same eval suite we use? we'll share a link to prompts and expected outputs.
06:06 Priya Shah: yes please share the prompt set; we'll run it against the hotfix and fallback variants and post diffs.
06:12 Jordan Blake: okay let's recap next steps — Redwood to push hotfix to canary 6/3, deliver rollback + rollout plan, provide logs and SOC2 excerpt, share scheduler and cache tuning docs. Nimbus will run soak tests and provide perf traces and confirm pilot scope for Dedicated pool.
06:30 Ava Reynolds: thanks everyone. appreciate the thoroughness. we'll reconvene after canary results; Marcus, please set the follow-up for 2026-06-09.
06:40 Marcus Liu: scheduling now, invite shortly.
06:46 Jordan Blake: thanks all. meeting adjourned.
